title: PromptBudgetProfile (EK-1 frozen admission specification)
description: Freezes the PromptBudgetProfile value defined by the plan section 'Bounded prompt and context envelope' EXACTLY: the property set below is the plan's field list, nothing more, nothing less. Every limit is a positive finite integer; zero, missing and unsupported limits fail closed (there is no unbounded representation in this schema: no null, no Infinity, no negative sentinel, no optional limit). Adding, renaming or re-typing a property reopens EK-1.

providerModelLimitTableRef.description: Read-only lookup over the exact provider/model/version already pinned on ActivityAttempt. It cannot select, reroute, fallback or infer a route; the artifact it references carries no selection semantics (see $defs/ProviderModelLimitTable).

providerContextLimitTokens.description: Context-window limit in tokens for the exact pinned provider/model/version. MUST equal the contextLimitTokens of the limit-table row keyed by that exact triple; zero, missing row or any inequality fails closed.

tokenCounterRef.description: Pinned counter contract: name and protocolVersion are frozen consts; the implementation is content-addressed. Counter drift (pinned digest != running digest) is a TOKEN_COUNTER_MISMATCH failure, never a silent recount.

maxProviderRequests.description: Upper bound on requestOrdinal for one ActivityAttempt. Admission law: requestOrdinal <= maxProviderRequests.

maxStaticTokens.description: Per-request cap on static layers (initial prompt frame, protocol skill, semantic skill, tool schemas, write-authority block, desk pointer). Static over-budget workshop packages fail installation/admission.

maxDynamicTokens.description: Per-request cap on dynamic semantic layers (task projection summary, workspace summary, hook additionalContext).

maxRecoveryTokens.description: Per-request cap on recovery layers (bounded recovery memory, prior-deaths list, bounded recovery feedback). Elite-3 law: accumulated gate feedback must never grow unboundedly across retries.

maxToolResultTokens.description: Per-request cap on retained tool results carried into the request.

maxTotalInputTokens.description: Per-request total input cap. Admission law: requestInputTokens <= min(maxTotalInputTokens, effectiveInputLimit) where effectiveInputLimit = providerContextLimitTokens - reservedOutputTokens - providerOverheadReserveTokens - safetyMarginTokens.

maxCumulativeSessionInputTokens.description: Session cumulative cap. Admission law: cumulativeInputTokens + requestInputTokens <= maxCumulativeSessionInputTokens. Coherence law: >= min(maxTotalInputTokens, effectiveInputLimit).

reservedOutputTokens.description: Reserved output space inside the context window. The transport enforces maxOutputTokens <= reservedOutputTokens or refuses the provider/model when no conservative output bound can be enforced.

providerOverheadReserveTokens.description: Reserve for provider-side request overhead not visible to the assembler.

safetyMarginTokens.description: Safety margin subtracted from the provider context limit before admission.

maxPromptBytes.description: Hard byte backstop over the fully serialized request. The successor of SAGA_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES with no unlimited representation: the baseline '?? 0 means UNLIMITED' behavior is forbidden.

PositiveFiniteInteger.description: A positive finite limit. 0, negative, fractional, null, missing, numeric strings and non-number sentinels are all invalid; unboundedness is not representable.

ContentRef.description: Content-addressed reference into the installed workshop manifest. Resolution is by digest, never by mutable path.

ProviderModelLimitTableRef.description: Reference (with digest) to an immutable ProviderModelLimitTable artifact. The table is read-only input to admission; it never selects a route.

ProviderModelLimitTable.description: Exact-key lookup artifact. Each row is keyed by the exact (provider, model, version) triple; wildcards ('*'), default rows, fallback chains, priority/order fields, eligibility rules and any route-selection field are structurally absent because additionalProperties is false everywhere and the key fields forbid '*'. Real production tables land at EK-8; examples under specs/examples/ are illustrative only.

encoding.description: Identity of the deterministic byte-to-token encoding the implementation applies (e.g. a named BPE merge table). Part of the pin: counter + encoding drift is a mismatch failure.

TokenCounterRef.description: The pinned token-counter contract. saga-token-counter-protocol v1 laws: (1) local pure function over the exact serialized request bytes, no network, clock or randomness; (2) identical bytes + identical pinned identity => identical counts on any machine; (3) counts the exact final serialized form admitted at the pre-send boundary; (4) identity is name+protocolVersion+encoding+implementation digest. Provider-reported usage is postflight evidence, never the admission oracle.
